title: Short Stuff: Bourgeoisie
summary: Short Stuff episode on the word "bougie" and its root "bourgeois"/"bourgeoisie." Hosts trace the word from its medieval French origin (bourg, a small town, where bourgeois meant the middle class of the time) through Moliere's 1670 comedy Le Bourgeois gentilhomme, which mocked social climbers, to Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels's 1848 Communist Manifesto, which recast the bourgeoisie as exploiters of the working class. They cover the IWW (Wobblies) slang "boushwa" that later became slang for bs, Gladys Knight and the Pips' 1980 disco hit "Bougie Bougie," and Migos' "Bad and Bougie," contrasting American put-down usage with the more neutral or positive sense in modern France, including the French tiers of bourgeois.

segments.title: Opening banter and pronunciation of bourgeois
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode and the word 'bougie' as a put-down, distinguishing the adjective/noun forms of bourgeois and bourgeoisie.

segments.title: Karl Marx and the Communist Manifesto
segments.summary: Marx and Engels in the 1848 Communist Manifesto adopted 'bourgeois' (originally 'bergerliche Gesellschaft' in German) for the owners of capital who exploited the proletariat.

segments.title: Wobblies and the slang boushwa
segments.summary: The term crossed to America in the early 20th century; the IWW (Wobblies) coined the slang 'boushwa', which later morphed into slang for nonsense or bs, per the Grammarphobia blog.

segments.title: Gladys Knight and the Pips' Bougie Bougie
segments.summary: The put-down sense of 'bougie' appears in Black culture, popularized by Gladys Knight and the Pips' 1980 disco hit 'Bougie Bougie' about a working-class person flaunting new wealth.

segments.title: Medieval origins and Moliere's comedy
segments.summary: Original French 'bourg' referred to a small town; bourgeois were the middle class above peasants. Moliere's 1670 comedy Le Bourgeois gentilhomme mocked a middle-class social climber.

segments.title: Migos and Bad and Bougie
segments.summary: Migos' 'Bad and Bougie' uses the spelling bougie in a proud, flaunting sense, unlike the put-down usage.

segments.title: Modern meaning in America vs France
segments.summary: In America 'bougie' is generally a put-down meaning basic or boring; in modern France it means well-mannered or educated, with tiers of Parisian bourgeois from nobility to petite bourgeois shopkeepers and artists.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts wrap up and plug the show's iHeartRadio distribution.
